title: Groq Raises $350M Series A After Earlier $650M Financing
summary: Groq’s latest official financing is a $350 million Series A led by Disruptive, with planned participation from Nvidia, bringing its recent funding to $1 billion.
body:
## Another round for the inference cloud

Groq announced a $350 million Series A on August 17, 2026, led by Disruptive, with planned participation from Nvidia. The round values the company at $3.5 billion. Together with the $650 million in growth capital announced in June, Groq says it has raised $1 billion in recent financing.

The company reports operating 13 data centers across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific. Its latest announcement puts its developer base at more than six million, up from the more than five million reported with the June financing.

The new round is separate from Groq’s December 2025 non-exclusive agreement licensing its inference technology to Nvidia. Under that agreement, founder Jonathan Ross, then-president Sunny Madra and other team members joined Nvidia, while Groq continued operating independently and GroqCloud remained available.

The relationship has since expanded. Nvidia incorporated Groq technology into its LPX inference platform, and Groq joined the Nvidia Cloud Partner program in August 2026. Groq says that status will support the future deployment of Nvidia accelerated-computing systems in its data centers. These developments should not be conflated: the licensing agreement, cloud-partner status and planned Nvidia participation in the Series A are distinct arrangements.

## Why it matters

The financing reinforces Groq’s shift toward operating a managed inference cloud rather than relying only on sales of its original accelerator technology. A cloud service gives developers direct access to inference capacity while placing responsibility for infrastructure, scheduling and utilization on Groq.

That model is capital intensive. Expanding capacity requires data-center space, power, networking and equipment before demand is fully realized. Groq says it is scaling beyond 200 megawatts as inference demand grows.

The company now occupies an unusual position: it remains an independent cloud operator while technology it developed is incorporated into Nvidia systems, and Nvidia is also expected to become an investor in its latest round. Groq’s next challenge is to turn the additional capital and deeper Nvidia relationship into reliable capacity and durable customer demand.
title_zh: Groq完成3.5亿美元A轮融资，近期融资总额达10亿美元
summary_zh: Groq最新正式融资为3.5亿美元A轮，由Disruptive领投，英伟达计划参投；加上6月融资，公司近期融资总额达到10亿美元。
body_zh:
## 推理云再获一轮融资

Groq于2026年8月17日宣布完成3.5亿美元A轮融资，由Disruptive领投，英伟达计划参与投资。本轮融资对公司的估值为35亿美元。加上6月宣布的6.5亿美元增长资金，Groq称其近期融资总额已达到10亿美元。

公司目前表示，其在北美、欧洲、中东和亚太地区运营13座数据中心。最新公告称Groq服务的开发者已超过600万，高于6月融资公告所披露的超过500万。

本轮融资与Groq在2025年12月同英伟达签署的非独家推理技术许可协议是两项独立交易。根据该许可协议，创始人Jonathan Ross、时任总裁Sunny Madra及其他部分团队成员加入英伟达；Groq继续作为独立公司运营，GroqCloud也继续提供服务。

双方关系此后进一步扩大。英伟达把Groq技术纳入LPX推理平台，Groq又于2026年8月加入英伟达云合作伙伴计划。Groq表示，这项认证将支持其未来在自有数据中心部署英伟达加速计算系统。技术许可、云合作伙伴身份以及英伟达计划参与A轮融资属于不同安排，不应合并为同一项交易。

## 为什么重要

这轮融资进一步强化了Groq向托管式推理云运营商转型的方向，而不再只依赖其原创加速器技术的销售。云服务能让开发者直接使用推理算力，同时由Groq负责基础设施、任务调度和设备利用率。

这种模式也十分消耗资本。扩充算力需要提前投入数据中心空间、电力、网络和设备，而客户需求未必会同步兑现。Groq目前表示，随着推理需求增长，公司正在把容量扩展到200兆瓦以上。

Groq如今处于一个较为特殊的位置：公司仍是独立云服务运营商，其研发的技术已被纳入英伟达系统，而英伟达又计划成为其最新一轮融资的投资者。Groq接下来需要证明，新增资本以及与英伟达更深入的关系能够转化为稳定算力和长期客户需求。
